---
title: "Hopf–Cole Cosmology"
subtitle: "From Burgers' equation to the cosmic web, in your browser"
toc: false
---

The **Hopf–Cole transform** turns the nonlinear Burgers equation into the
linear heat equation. That single trick connects shock formation, the
Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation, Feynman's path integral, and the formation of
cosmic structure: with the growth factor as the clock, cold dark matter in
the Zel'dovich approximation moves exactly according to Burgers' equation,
and the *adhesion model* of the cosmic web is its viscous version.

These notes build the subject up from a lecture on Fourier methods for
Burgers' equation to a working two- and three-dimensional cosmological
solver that compares **Lagrangian perturbation theory to fourth order**
(rendered as a phase-space sheet) with the **Hopf–Cole spectral solution**,
side by side in real space and Fourier space. Everything is computed live in
the browser with WebAssembly and drawn with WebGPU.

## What you will learn

- Why the heat equation is "trivial" in Fourier space and "local" in real
  space, and why having both views at once is so powerful.
- How a change of variables moves all the mode coupling of a nonlinear
  equation into an exponential and a logarithm.
- Why the Zel'dovich approximation is Burgers' equation, and how the adhesion
  model builds a cosmic web from a Fourier multiplier.
- How to go beyond Zel'dovich with a general $n$-th order Lagrangian
  perturbation theory recursion, and what a phase-space sheet is.
- What mode coupling looks like in a Fourier amplitude map, what one-loop
  perturbation theory predicts for the power spectrum, and why the effective
  field theory of large-scale structure needs a counterterm.

## Requirements

The interactive panels need a modern browser with WebAssembly. WebGPU
(Chrome, Edge, Safari 26, Firefox 141+) gives the fastest rendering; without
it the pages fall back to Canvas2D. The 3D mode at $128^3$ needs about
1 GB of memory.

The source, including the Rust numerical core and this text, is at
[github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology).
